question: Does a Random Forest beat VaidyaAI's liver rules on held-out patients?

dataset.source: UCI Machine Learning Repository, id 225 (ILPD), downloaded 2026-10-06
dataset.label_note: 'Non liver patient' means the hospital did not record liver disease, not that the person is healthy. Kept exactly as published.
dataset.resampling: none -- class weights only, no SMOTE, no oversampling

rules.how_run: the real VaidyaAI validator + rule engine, fused with merge_decision_set; no printed limit (the dataset has none), so the rules' fallback limits apply

app_inputs_model.threshold_basis: lowest out-of-fold threshold whose specificity on the TRAINING portion is at least the rules' specificity on that same portion
app_inputs_model.ship_criterion: 95% interval of (model - rules) sensitivity entirely above zero, AND model specificity >= rules specificity - 0.05

paper_only_model_with_alp_albumin.threshold_basis: lowest out-of-fold threshold whose specificity on the TRAINING portion is at least the rules' specificity on that same portion
paper_only_model_with_alp_albumin.ship_criterion: 95% interval of (model - rules) sensitivity entirely above zero, AND model specificity >= rules specificity - 0.05

app_inputs_model.note: Point estimates per split; the per-split bootstrap is not repeated. 'Meeting criterion point estimates' is LOOSER than the real ship criterion (which needs the sensitivity interval above zero), so it is an upper bound on how often the model would have shipped.

paper_only_model_with_alp_albumin.note: Point estimates per split; the per-split bootstrap is not repeated. 'Meeting criterion point estimates' is LOOSER than the real ship criterion (which needs the sensitivity interval above zero), so it is an upper bound on how often the model would have shipped.
